requiredFindings.title: Cargo table sorting changes first-wins behavior for colliding entry identifiers
requiredFindings.description: Flattening (source,name) as patch.<source>.<name> is not injective. Distinct patch tables can produce the same entry string. B3-b0 traverses document order and keeps the first entry; the Rust table iteration uses key order, so it can keep the other entry and declare a different member. LD-3 therefore does not establish order independence.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Preserve the reference's entry selection for colliding flattened identifiers, including source document order where it affects first-wins. Add a reference-derived collision control using quoted dotted source/name keys in opposite document/key order, and update LD-3. Do not silently add a package-key grammar restriction to eliminate the case.

requiredFindings.title: Branch-A batching observes later failures before deciding the first 6b refusal
requiredFindings.description: phase_two checks directory custody for the whole observable prefix and calls member_verdicts for that prefix before inspecting any 6b verdict. For candidates a,b, an ordinary 6b refusal at a should end branch A in B3-b0, but later custody observation errors or native 6b I/O/budget failure at b can instead escape through O::Error. It also spends work on later members after a terminal refusal. The infallible vector adapter cannot expose this difference.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Provide branch-A short-circuit observation/decision order: directory custody and 6b for each candidate in path order, stopping at the first refusal while maintaining one pass-level environment/global-source check. Add a fallible/recording adapter control where a refuses and b would error or exhaust the budget, and assert b is not observed. Branch B may continue as its disclosure semantics require.

requiredFindings.title: The observation adapter does not record directory listings
requiredFindings.description: Synthetic::children reads and returns names without recording any call or path. The access subset/forbidden checks inspect only consulted and read, so a children call below a pruned anchor or boundary can be made and discarded without changing outputs or failing an access assertion. A2 explicitly requires recording entry, markers, children and bytes calls.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Record and validate listing access separately or through an equivalent observation record, preserving the reference's allowed listing scope and forbidden paths. Add an output-preserving mutation that lists a forbidden subtree; the current metadata-lookup mutation does not cover this method.

requiredFindings.title: JSON alignment controls omit the required byte-bound cases
requiredFindings.description: The 26 JSON controls cover 13 values for carriers/providers, but none is at or beyond the 4-MiB byte bound required by A2 r2. They do not exercise the TooLarge path or the custody/read/parser boundary at that limit.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Add carrier and provider JSON controls exactly at and beyond 4 MiB, with appropriate metadata and actual bytes, and compare the reference/product dispositions. Preserve custody-before-read precedence where metadata already refuses, and cover a bounded read reporting TooLarge when applicable. Refresh case counts, generated pins and evidence.
